result.summary: Hassabis was still a UCL researcher in 2012 and DeepMind was in stealth, so there is little public record from that year. The one piece in his own words, his 'Model the brain's algorithms' section of a February 2012 Nature comment, argues that neuroscience can guide AI but gives no date or time span. No dated or undated AGI timeline from 2012 was found.

reply_text:
Open the Nature piece.The PDF link appeared on a page I opened; fetch it.I found no dated AI predictions from Demis Hassabis in 2012. All three fixed searches ran once each, and I used all 12 searches and 4 of the 6 page openings.

- **The one 2012 text in his own words** is his short piece "Model the brain's algorithms". It was published on 22 February 2012 in *Nature* as part of a four-author Turing centenary comment, "Is the brain a good model for machine intelligence?" Nature's own page and PDF link gave only the metadata (`meta-access: No`), so I couldn't read it there. I got the full text from a scan of the printed pages posted on a lab blog (molpit.org). His section argues that neuroscience can inspire new AI algorithms and that AI researchers should run brain experiments. It names no year or length of time and doesn't say when general AI might arrive. I read his section in full and nothing qualified.
- **The fixed searches** turned up only recent coverage (2024–2026) of his current timelines, such as AGI by 2030 or in five to ten years. None of it is from 2012.
- **Later retellings of 2012** don't count for this year. Those include accounts of his 2012 meeting with Elon Musk and his recollection of DeepMind's 2012 Pong experiments. I only saw these in search results and didn't open them.
- **Other years:** his 2010 Singularity Summit talk on a neuroscience route to AGI is listed in talk indexes, but I didn't open it. His 2010 and 2011 talks may be a better place to look for early timeline statements than 2012.
